title: The Moon's shape from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter: gridded radius at 4 and 16 pixels per degree, with the count of laser shots in each pixel (the finer grids read on demand)
provider: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, LRO LOLA team (D. E. Smith), distributed by the PDS Geosciences Node, Washington University in St. Louis
format: PDS3 IMG, simple cylindrical, pixel-registered, little-endian 16-bit integers, one row per 1/ppd degree from 90 N, columns from 0 E eastward to 360 E. LDEM: height = DN x 0.5 m above a sphere of 1737.4 km (the radius less 1737.4 km). LDEC: the number of LOLA shots in each pixel; zero where the grid was filled by GMT's surface (tension 0.5). Frame: the Moon's mean-Earth/polar-axis frame of DE421, which MOON_ME of DE440 follows. The grids at 64 and 128 ppd at the same address (LDEM_64 and LDEC_64, 531 MB each; LDEM_128 and LDEC_128, 2.1 GB each) are read by the data library's tile service in blocks of 128 x 512 pixels by HTTP multi-range requests, and kept in data/cache/lola-gdr/blocks/.
coverage: The whole Moon; LDEM_4 at 7.6 km, LDEM_16 at 1.9 km, LDEM_64 at 474 m, LDEM_128 at 237 m per pixel at the equator. Laser tracks are dense toward the poles and kilometres apart near the equator; LDEC says where.
licence: NASA data, freely available without restriction; cite the reference below.
citation: Smith, D. E., et al. (2010), The Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter investigation on the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter mission, Space Science Reviews 150, 209-241; LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, NASA Planetary Data System, PDS Geosciences Node.
